Acetaminophen safety: 5

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient presents soon after a potentially toxic acetaminophen ingestion but feels well and wants to leave. Which principle explains why timely assessment should not depend only on the presence of early symptoms?

  1. Analgesic and antipyretic effects with limited peripheral anti-inflammatory action
  2. NAPQI-mediated hepatic injury
  3. N-acetylcysteine
  4. Unintentional duplicate acetaminophen exposure
  5. Early absence of symptoms does not exclude toxic exposure
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Early absence of symptoms does not exclude toxic exposure

Acetaminophen toxicity can be initially subtle; suspected overdose requires timely toxicology assessment.

Understanding the options

Early absence of symptoms does not exclude toxic exposure
Acetaminophen toxicity can be initially subtle; suspected overdose requires timely toxicology assessment.
Analgesic and antipyretic effects with limited peripheral anti-inflammatory action
Acetaminophen treats pain and fever but does not provide the same peripheral anti-inflammatory action as conventional NSAIDs. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
NAPQI-mediated hepatic injury
Excess acetaminophen can overwhelm glutathione detoxification of the reactive metabolite NAPQI. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
N-acetylcysteine
N-acetylcysteine supports glutathione-dependent detoxification and is the antidote used for acetaminophen poisoning. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Unintentional duplicate acetaminophen exposure
Combination cold and pain products can contain acetaminophen, creating overdose risk when totals are not reconciled. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
